01 / 060:00 to 0:20Abigail

Transparent crowdfunding

Good evening everyone. We are Team Kairos. Kairos is a transparent crowdfunding platform for people who want to help but need to know what happened to their money. Every donor should be able to follow their contribution.

DELIVERY NOTEIntroduce the promise, then move into the school-fee example.
37 spoken wordsNext: The trust gap and our first users
02 / 060:20 to 0:45Abigail

The trust gap and our first users

Our first users are students who need help with fees and the people funding those bills. When an appeal arrives on WhatsApp, a donor asks: is the bill real, how much is owed, and will my money actually reach the school? That hesitation is the problem.

DELIVERY NOTEKeep the student and donor in the story. Leave a brief pause after the questions.
46 spoken wordsNext: Features that work today
03 / 060:45 to 1:20Abigail

Features that work today

The live AI interview turns the story into a cause with a named provider and an itemised budget. The organiser can upload evidence, and someone can give through the shared link without an account. Contributions update the cause and public ledger. The organiser can request payment against that bill, but has no personal withdrawal path.

DELIVERY NOTEExplain the working flow. The separate demo shows it. Real custody and settlement remain unbuilt.
55 spoken wordsNext: Technical approach and donor accounting
04 / 061:20 to 2:00Abigail

Technical approach and donor accounting

Technically, Next.js handles the app, Anthropic powers the interview, MongoDB stores the records, and Cloudinary stores uploads. The server checks the available balance and budget before recording a payout.

A donor doesn't just get a thank you, they get a receipt which tells them exactly what their money was used for. This table shows each donor's share of the school-fee payment. Upkeep is disclosed before giving.

DELIVERY NOTEDwell on the server checks and one donor row. These figures are application records, not real school settlement.
66 spoken wordsNext: Feasibility and responsible innovation
05 / 062:00 to 2:45Abigail

Feasibility and responsible innovation

The working code demonstrates the flow. Identity checks and settlement are simulated. Real funds still require a licensed custody partner, live identity checks and provider-confirmed settlement.

Published attachments are public today; sensitive evidence needs private review. Our planned exception flow pauses an expired reference, requests a replacement and escalates unresolved checks to a human. A human should make the final decision on unresolved checks.

DELIVERY NOTETake time here. Separate present safeguards from proposed privacy, reference replacement and human review.
64 spoken wordsNext: Validation and next steps
06 / 062:45 to 3:20Abigail

Validation and next steps

So far, validation is internal: guest donations, uploads, budget limits and donor allocations have been tested. Walkthrough feedback helped us improve the interview and verification flow.

Next is a small school-fee pilot with students, donors and an institution, recording what they understand and what we change. Thank you.

DELIVERY NOTEInternal testing is not external user validation. The donor/institution pilot is still proposed. Finish at 3:20; the demo is separate.

Kairos makes crowdfunding transparent. A published need and itemised budget name the provider to be paid; each donor can follow their own contribution through the cause records.

The live AI interview, uploads, internal accounting and notifications work. Identity lookup and settlement in this demonstration are simulated; licensed partners and private evidence review are still needed.

Our next step is a small school-fee pilot with students, donors and an institution, using actual findings to improve the flow.

18 of 18 questions
What does Kairos do?Rehearse first001 · The giving flow

It connects a published need and budget to provider payments and each donor's share. The prototype implements the accounting and updates; live custody and settlement still require integration.

What stops the organizer withdrawing donations?Rehearse first002 · The giving flow

The prototype has no personal cash-withdrawal path and checks payment permissions, balance and budget. Live operation needs a licensed custody/payment arrangement that enforces the same restrictions.

Does the receipt independently prove the school received money?Rehearse first003 · The giving flow

The current receipt records a simulated application payout. A live settled receipt must be tied to confirmed provider settlement; a locally generated invoice alone is insufficient.

Can someone give without an account?004 · The giving flow

Yes. Guest gifts are anonymous and appear in the public cause records. Signed-in donors can receive personal in-app updates; email is optional.

What if a Remita reference expires?Rehearse first005 · Review and privacy

The agreed proposed flow pauses payout, asks the organizer through the AI for a replacement, verifies the same student, institution and bill, then continues. This is not yet implemented.

When does a human step in?Rehearse first006 · Review and privacy

The proposed workflow escalates a mismatch or an unresolved check. The reviewer checks evidence, records the decision and permits an appropriate next step. A dedicated reviewer workflow is not built.

Does AI authenticate documents or identify fraud?Rehearse first007 · Review and privacy

It helps structure the need and can discuss consistency. Uploads are accepted supporting material. Independent document authentication, image-reuse checks and live registry checks are not operational.

Who can view supporting files today?Rehearse first008 · Review and privacy

Unpublished files are owner-only. Files attached to published causes are publicly viewable through the app. Sensitive evidence needs a separate access/redaction design before live use.

Do you store a donor's or organizer's NIN?009 · Review and privacy

The current identity endpoint stores the simulated verification result and method, not the NIN number. This does not establish that live identity verification or a complete launch privacy program is in place.

How does the fee cap work?Rehearse first010 · Fees and records

The current rule takes 2% of each gross gift until total upkeep reaches ₦5,000 for that cause. It is a per-cause cap. The charge and net cause credit are shown before confirmation.

How are donor shares calculated?Rehearse first011 · Fees and records

The allocation uses the donor's net contribution after upkeep. In the full school-fee example, Abigail's ₦155,000 gross payment credits ₦153,000 and that net amount is attributed to the school's recorded payout.

Have you reconciled real bank payments?Rehearse first012 · Fees and records

No. Internal balances and payment allocations run in the prototype. External reconciliation needs unique references and a match to confirmed provider settlement, including pending, failed and duplicate events.

Is NGO funding already secured?013 · Fees and records

No. Donations and NGO grants are the intended primary support, with tentative capped upkeep as a fallback. The prototype currently applies its upkeep rule; no grant-triggered switch or proven unit economics is claimed.

Are refunds implemented?014 · Fees and records

A complete production refund and dispute process is still to be designed and integrated. The prototype does not prove that operation.

What user research supports this presentation?Rehearse first015 · Evidence and launch

The supplied materials contain the team's school-fee observation, but no documented interview findings were provided for this draft. The team should add actual dated findings and their design implications before claiming user validation.

What would the first pilot measure?016 · Evidence and launch

Start with school-fee bills settled, donor understanding of receipts, unresolved payment issues and repeat giving. These are proposed measures, not completed pilot results.

What remains before live donations?Rehearse first017 · Evidence and launch

Licensed custody and live payments, independent verification, appropriate private-evidence controls, external reconciliation and an exception/refund process. No signed custody partnership is claimed.

How long is this pitch allowed to be?018 · Evidence and launch

The confirmed format is one minute for team introduction, seven minutes for presentation and demo, five minutes for Q&A and two minutes for scoring/transition. The user has allocated three minutes and twenty seconds to the pitch; demo timing is separate.

Keep these distinctions clear

  • Working: prototype accounting, budget checks, attribution, notifications and public history.
  • Simulated: bank transfer, Remita settlement and NIN lookup.
  • Unbuilt: live CAC and account-name checks, general upload verification and the complete production operating flow.
  • Not signed: licensed custody and payments partnership.
  • User evidence: Current validation is internal walkthroughs and isolated flow/accounting tests. A student/donor/institution pilot is the next step, not a completed result.

Delivery, in the JCI spirit

  • Use the original school-fees story. Let the hesitation land.
  • Explain the case, provider payment and receipt before discussing integrations.
  • Read the donor's numbers slowly. Leave a beat for the receipt.
  • Choose Abigail or Ugochukwu as lead. The opening and team introduction follow that choice; both remain on the team slide.
  • Answer the question first. Add one piece of evidence, then stop.
  • If a technical detail is uncertain, check it. Keep the simulated parts explicit.
